source.description: Project command-line parser point where attacker-controlled --pin option text is accepted and bound to opt_pin.
source.note: The fuzz target constructs argv from bytes, but the scored source is the OpenSC tool option parser consuming optarg for OPT_PIN.

taint_source.description: Attacker-controlled CLI PIN value enters OpenSC state as opt_pin.
taint_source.note: optarg is caller-owned argv storage; util_get_pin does not allocate a new buffer for ordinary PIN strings.

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant value: util_get_pin stores the caller-owned input pointer directly in opt_pin.
tainted_value_origin.note: For non-env input, util_get_pin aliases opt_pin to input instead of returning owned heap storage.

sink.description: ASan crash location: change_pin frees pincode even when it aliases opt_pin/caller-owned argv storage.

root_cause.description: Root cause: the empty-PIN error path unconditionally frees pincode. When pincode came from opt_pin, it aliases command-line argument storage and is not owned by change_pin; only a PIN returned by get_pin should be freed here.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses attacker-controlled command-line options and stores the --pin argument into opt_pin.
For ordinary non-env PIN input, aliases opt_pin to the argv/optarg string rather than allocating owned memory.
Executes change_pin when the parsed action is --change-pin.
On empty PIN, treats pincode as owned and frees it despite opt_pin being non-NULL.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled --pin option is parsed by OpenSC and passed to util_get_pin.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The OpenSC pkcs15-tool option parser accepts an attacker-controlled --pin argument and stores it in global opt_pin. util_get_pin aliases ordinary PIN text directly to the caller-provided optarg; it does not allocate a buffer. change_pin then assigns pincode = opt_pin. If the supplied PIN is empty, the error branch calls free(pincode) unconditionally, even though pincode aliases opt_pin/caller-owned argument storage. This causes an invalid free. The same function already frees pincode conditionally in other paths, showing the intended ownership rule.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch wraps the empty-PIN free with if (opt_pin == NULL). That preserves freeing only for pincode values returned by get_pin, which allocates input interactively, and avoids freeing caller-owned opt_pin strings supplied through the command line.
